hypothesis: Lollapalooza: iterations scoring >= 90 have structurally different thesis-term distributions from iterations at 70-89
falsifier: KS p > 0.05 for every feature => REFUTED
verdict_detail: No structural feature shows a statistically significant difference (all p > 0.05) between high-scoring (>=90) and mid-scoring (70-89) iterations. Per the pre-registered falsifier in seam section 9 P1, the Lollapalooza hypothesis is refuted: high-scoring iterations do not exhibit detectably different structural signatures from mid-scoring ones on the features tested.
anti_overfitting_notes: thesis_primitive_names is only populated for the best iteration per project; most records use regex fallback.
active_constraints reflects current rubric state, not historical state at iteration time.
High bucket N=93 is adequate for KS but smaller than mid bucket N=296.
